mekki-muskil:9-9.t:
His saying, Exalted is He, يَوْم تمور السَّمَاء مورا: the governing word in يوم is واقع, i.e. "the punishment of your Lord will surely occur on the day the heaven sways" (إن عذاب ربك لواقع يوم تمور السماء). دافع does not govern it, because what is negated does not govern what comes before the negating particle: you do not say طعامَك ما زيد آكلا ("your food, Zayd is not eating"), whether you put آكلا in the nominative or the accusative or bring the بـ onto it. But if you put الطعام in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and make آكلا fall upon a هاء [referring to it], it is permissible, and what follows الطعام is its khabar (predicate); and omitting the هاء is ugly.
His saying فويل للمكذبين: a mubtadaʾ (subject) governing يومئذ, and للمكذبين is the khabar (predicate). The فاء is the answer to the preceding sentence, and that is good because the speech contains the sense of a condition, since the meaning is "when what was mentioned comes to pass, then woe that day to the deniers".

mekki-muskil:14-14.t: His saying هَذِه النَّار: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), [the whole] spoken [by an implied saying]; its implied form is "it will be said to them: this is the Fire" (يقال لهم هذه النار). Like it in the implying of the saying is His saying كلوا واشربوا, i.e. "it will be said to them: eat and drink".

mekki-muskil:19-19.t: His saying هَنِيئًا: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun).

mekki-muskil:29-29.t: His saying بكاهن وَلَا مَجْنُون: in ordinary speech the accusative is permissible by conjunction with the position of بكاهن in the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz, and the nominative is permissible by conjunction with the position of بكاهن in the dialect of Banū Tamīm, and by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "nor is he mad" (ولا هو مجنون).

mekki-muskil:44-44.t:
His saying سَحَاب مركوم: nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "this is a cloud" (هذا سحاب).
His saying يَوْم لَا يُغني: يوم is accusative as a badal (substitute) of يومهم, and يومهم is accusative by يلاقوا as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); its accusative is not as an adverb.

mekki-muskil:45-45.t: His saying فذرهم: its origin is فاوذرهم, but the wāw was omitted because it has the meaning of فدعهم, so it was treated like its counterpart in meaning and like what stands in its place, because they dispensed with the use of ودع by their saying ترك; likewise وذرهم was not used, just as ودع was not used. The wāw was omitted from يدع only because it is on the pattern of يزن, the دال being like the زاي in vowelling; but the دال in يدع was given a fatḥa because of the guttural letter after it, and its origin is the kasra, like the زاي of يزن. So the wāw was omitted according to the rule, because it falls between a yāʾ and a kasra, and it was omitted from يذر because it has the meaning of يدع. The mention of this has preceded.

mekki-muskil:49-49.t: His saying وإدبار النُّجُوم: إدبار is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān); its implied form is "and glorify Him at the time of the stars' retreating" (وسبحه وقت إدبار النجوم). Like it is وإدبار السجود in the reading of whoever gives the hamza a kasra. As for whoever gives it a fatḥa in [Sūrat] Qāf, he made it the plural of دُبُر, which is an adverb used with latitude; it is related from the Arabs: جئتك دبر الصلاة ("I came to you after the prayer"). All of this is only by omission of "time" (وقت), just as you say جئتك مقدم الحاج وخفوق النجم ("I came to you at the arrival of the pilgrims and the setting of the star"), i.e. at the time of that.
